doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Siblings and his mother as a Baptist church pianist
summary: Harris was the fourth of five children. His mother Bessie played church piano and could follow any key.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes. Do you have any siblings?

Oh yes, um. I had three sisters and a bother, so it’s five of us. Right now – we lost two, so there are three of us left. Both older than me, so they were in their eighties. I’m eighty, my brother might be eighty-two, my sister might be eighty-four, eighty-five, you know. So we’re all in our eighties, you know.
What number are you in the family?
I was the um, one, two, three, four – the fourth one, my little sister was the fifth. So I was fourth, you know.
Okay. What kind of um, relationship did you have with your parents?
A pretty good relationship, you know. Mostly my mother, you know. My mother was a pianist, so I got started through my mother. So I say that I was closer to her, you know, because of the piano.
And what kind of piano did she play? What style, or what genre?

She was a church pianist, my brother. She was one of them Baptist players. Not one of those Baptist piano players today. Positively not the same. Um, pianists today, they sound like – they sound more like sanctified. Santified was different, ‘cause sanctified had drums, bass, um tambourine. The Baptist Church didn’t have none of that, you know. Um, so that – my mother was a good pianist too, you know. She was one of them pianists, man – you start singing, she starts playing.
Any key. No matter what you start singing, she’s right with you. So, she was – she was pretty hip, you know.
